newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Few Yugo firms expect exports in Q3 - poll.
newsitem.headline: Few Yugo firms expect exports in Q3 - poll.

text.p: A large number of Yugoslav firms do not plan to export in the next three months, which is worrying in view of the large trade deficit, the Belgrade- based Economics Institute said in its monthly report on Wednesday.

"Some 42.6 percent of firms polled in May and 40.5 percent in June are not planning to export in the next three months," the institute, which conducts a monthly poll among 300 industrial and energy sector firms, said in its report.
The Yugoslav first half 1997 trade gap was $1.084 billion, with exports standing at $1.028 billion and imports at $2.112 billion, according to official statistics.

"Exports are stagnating while imports were slightly lower than before, but we will end the year with a trade deficit certainly higher than last year's," said Miroljub Labus, a leading economist with the institute.
Businessmen maintained the optimism of May and April on the situation at their firms, with 28.1 percent expecting an improvement, 7.1 a deterioration, and the rest no change.
The general business climate in firms is seen as unfavourable, especially in the state-owned sector.
Capacity use dropped slightly in June to 54.37 percent from 57.52 percent in May.
The firms list as dominant restrictions to raising production the lack of credits (41.9 percent), low demand (27.4 percent) and shortage of raw materials (22.3 percent).

Inflationary expectations have been on a downward trend since the beginning of January, but the number of firms that expect prices to grow in the next three months is still very high, the report said without specifying.
Retail prices dropped 0.1 percent in June against May, when they rose just 0.2 percent on the previous month.
Investment prospects are dampened by high risk, lack of capital for long term investments and lack of access to international financial organisations.
In June, 30 percent of the firms saw realistic chances for investments from domestic sources, while 8.5 percent consider foreign sources will be available.
Although firms said the level of internal debts remained more or less the same in June, they expected debts to be reduced and claims to rise slightly in the coming period.
Accumulated 1997 inter-company debts in Yugoslavia have risen to 8.8 billion dinars ($1.48 billion, according to the central bank's Accounting and Payments Operations Office.
